body.zh-HK:
> 面試官問：「你的 agent 記得某位使用者上次說『這類 request 可以直接處理』。下一次相似 request 到來時，它可否直接沿用？你會怎樣設計 memory？」
>
> 答啱一半嘅答案：「把每段對話放進 vector database，檢索到相似內容就當成長期記憶。」

## 記得，不等於仍然可以使用

Agent memory 可以讓互動較連貫，但它不是天然的 source of truth，更不是 policy engine。上次對話的偏好、一次性的批准、文件中的事實、人工決定和目前的權限，壽命完全不同。把它們全放在同一個 embedding index，日後相似地撈出來，就可能把過期的例外當成永久規則、把另一個 tenant 的偏好帶過來、把已刪除或撤回的資料重新注入 context，或讓一段沒有 owner 的模型摘要壓過正式來源。

先將 memory 分類：session working memory 只服務當次工作；明確使用者 preference 可有較長 TTL，但須有 subject、scope 和可更正方式；evidence memory 必須保留 source ID、version、effective／expiry date 和 permission check；decision memory 必須有 owner、approval／review date 和撤銷條件；不確定、敏感或沒有明確用途的原文不應預設永久保存。每次 retrieval 都再次檢查 subject／tenant、role、purpose、scope、time、source status 和 deletion marker。查到舊條目，正確行為可能是不用它、要求更新、或只用作提出問題，而不是默默套用。

## 便利貼不能自動變成公司政策

便利貼可以幫你記得「今日會議改到三點」，但下星期它不會自動變成公司規定。若上面沒有日期、寫的人和適用範圍，貼得越久反而越危險。memory 是有期限、可追溯的提醒，不是永不過期的規章。

## 答案在哪裡會變薄

不要一開始建向量資料庫、長期個人檔案和自動跨 session recall。最小 baseline 是在同一 session 內保存一份經使用者看過的短摘要，session 結束便刪除或失效；需要長期資料時，先由一小組可檢查的 structured preferences 開始。若工作不需要跨 session continuity，最好的 memory design 可能是沒有長期 memory。

## 技術判斷：每一條記憶也要有生命週期

Memory record 至少需要：memory ID、class、subject／tenant、scope、purpose、source／decision reference、created_at、effective_at、expires_at、retrieved_at、policy version、owner、deletion status 和 confidence／provenance label。模型摘要若無法回到來源，應只被視為 provisional note，不能做授權、行動或高影響結論的依據。TTL 不能只在 storage job 裡「希望會刪」；retrieval path 也要 fail closed，對 expired、revoked、wrong-scope 或 deleted 記憶不回傳內容。

測試包括：同一 subject 的未過期 preference；已過期一次性批准；不同 tenant 的高相似文本；被使用者刪除的記憶；正式 policy 更新後舊摘要；以及 retriever 回傳空集合時 agent 的安全回答。expected result 要說明可否用、可否只作澄清問題、需要問誰和 audit receipt 要留甚麼。

## 工程層面：retrieval 需要撤銷與更正路徑

將寫入、搜尋、讀取和刪除／撤銷拆開。寫入時檢查用途和最小資料；讀取時加 permission + TTL + deletion filter；刪除時不只是 UI 上隱藏，而是令記憶不可再被 retrieval service 回傳，並在需要的範圍移除索引／cache。對已發出的模型輸出，記錄當時用過的 memory receipt，方便調查；不要為可追溯而永久保留全部敏感原文。

Decision memory 要和正式 policy source 分開。它可指出「這件 case 曾被誰處理」，但新 request 仍要用目前 policy 再判斷。若必須復用一個例外，應重新獲得 approval，而不是讓相似度分數替代 owner 的確認。

## 交付、業務與風險：使用者要能知道與改正系統記得甚麼

產品 owner 要決定哪些 continuity 真正有價值；資料／私隱 owner 定義 retention、deletion 和 access；流程 owner 處理 correction 與 dispute。量度 memory retrieval rate、expired／revoked block、cross-scope attempt、correction time、刪除完成狀態、因沒有記憶而需要補問的比例，以及從記憶導致的錯誤 suggestion。不要把「記得更多」當成目標；可安全地忘記、可說明沒有使用舊資料，也是一種品質。

## 可放進 portfolio 的 artefact

建立 expiring-agent-memory-lab：

- schemas/memory-record.json：class、scope、TTL、owner、provenance 和 deletion fields。
- fixtures/memories.json：完全合成的 session note、有效 preference、expired approval、wrong-tenant、revoked 和 source-updated memory。
- tests/retrieval-lifecycle.md：每個 request 的 expected admitted IDs、block reason、handoff 和 audit receipt。
- docs/deletion-and-correction.md：如何發出 delete、如何令 cache／index 失效、如何記錄更正而不公開敏感內容。
- docs/decision-record.md：為何 first release 採 session-only memory，哪些被量度的需要才可支持長期記憶。

## 延伸閱讀

[Agent draft 不作有後果 action](/zh-HK/interview-lab/agent-draft-without-consequential-actions)、[RAG：檢索、生成還是權限問題？](/zh-HK/interview-lab/rag-retrieval-generation-or-permission) 和 [Conflicting sources 需要 owner](/zh-HK/interview-lab/conflicting-sources-need-an-owner)。

## 範圍說明

這是 AI.DOG 的單題練習。memory、使用者、policy、刪除和結果全為虛構或 synthetic draft fixture；它不是私隱、保留或法律意見，亦不代表任何已部署記憶系統或商業成果。

body.en:
> Interviewer asks: “Your agent remembers that a user previously said ‘this kind of request can be handled directly’. When a similar request arrives later, may it reuse that memory? How would you design memory?”
>
> Half-right answer: “Put every conversation into a vector database and treat a similar retrieval as long-term memory.”

## Remembering does not mean it is still usable

Agent memory can make interaction more coherent, but it is not automatically a source of truth or a policy engine. A previous preference, one-time approval, document fact, human decision, and current permission have very different lifetimes. Put them all in one embedding index and retrieve similar text later, and you can turn an expired exception into a permanent rule, carry a preference across tenants, reintroduce deleted or revoked data into context, or let an ownerless model summary override an official source.

Classify memory first. Session working memory serves only the current task. An explicit user preference may have a longer TTL, but needs a subject, scope, and correction path. Evidence memory needs a source ID, version, effective and expiry date, and permission check. Decision memory needs an owner, approval or review date, and revocation condition. Uncertain, sensitive, or purposeless raw content should not become permanent by default. On every retrieval, recheck subject or tenant, role, purpose, scope, time, source status, and deletion marker. When an old item is found, the right behaviour may be to ignore it, ask for an update, or use it only to ask a question—not silently apply it.

## A sticky note cannot become company policy

A sticky note can remind you that today's meeting moved to three. It does not become company policy next week. Without a date, author, and scope, the longer it stays on the wall, the more dangerous it becomes. Memory is an expiring, traceable reminder, not an eternal rule book.

## Where an answer goes thin

Do not begin with a vector database, a permanent personal profile, and automatic cross-session recall. The smallest baseline is a short summary seen by the user within one session, deleted or expired at the session end. If long-lived data is needed, start with a small inspectable set of structured preferences. If the work does not benefit from cross-session continuity, the best memory design may have no long-term memory at all.

## Technical judgement: every memory has a lifecycle

A memory record needs at least memory ID, class, subject or tenant, scope, purpose, source or decision reference, created_at, effective_at, expires_at, retrieved_at, policy version, owner, deletion status, and confidence or provenance label. A model summary that cannot lead back to source material is only a provisional note; it must not authorise action or support a high-impact conclusion. TTL cannot be a storage job that you merely hope deletes data. The retrieval path itself must fail closed and return no content for expired, revoked, wrong-scope, or deleted memory.

Tests should include a current preference for the same subject, an expired one-time approval, highly similar text from a different tenant, user-deleted memory, an old summary after an official policy update, and a retrieval that returns nothing. The expected result should state whether the item may be used, whether it may only trigger a clarification question, who to ask, and what audit receipt remains.

## Engineering implementation: retrieval needs revocation and correction paths

Separate write, search, read, and delete or revoke operations. At write time, check purpose and data minimisation. At read time, apply permission, TTL, and deletion filters. Deletion must do more than hide a UI item: the retrieval service must stop returning it, and relevant index or cache entries must be invalidated. For a model answer already issued, retain the minimal memory receipt used at that time for investigation; do not keep all sensitive raw text forever in the name of traceability.

Decision memory remains distinct from an official policy source. It can say “someone handled a related case before”, but a new request must still be evaluated under the current policy. If an exception must be reused, obtain approval again instead of letting a similarity score substitute for an owner's confirmation.

## Delivery, business, and risk

A product owner decides which continuity is genuinely valuable. A data or privacy owner defines retention, deletion, and access. A process owner handles correction and dispute. Measure memory-retrieval rate, expired and revoked blocks, cross-scope attempts, correction time, deletion completion, the share of cases that need a follow-up because no memory was used, and bad suggestions caused by memory. “Remember more” is not the goal. Safely forgetting and being able to explain that old data was not used are quality properties too.

## A portfolio artefact someone can inspect

Build expiring-agent-memory-lab with:

- schemas/memory-record.json: class, scope, TTL, owner, provenance, and deletion fields.
- fixtures/memories.json: fully synthetic session notes, current preferences, expired approvals, wrong-tenant, revoked, and source-updated memory.
- tests/retrieval-lifecycle.md: expected admitted IDs, block reason, handoff, and audit receipt for each request.
- docs/deletion-and-correction.md: how deletion is requested, how cache and index are invalidated, and how corrections are recorded without exposing sensitive content.
- docs/decision-record.md: why the first release uses session-only memory and what measured need would justify long-term memory.

## Further reading

[Agent drafts without consequential actions](/en/interview-lab/agent-draft-without-consequential-actions), [RAG: a retrieval, generation, or permission problem?](/en/interview-lab/rag-retrieval-generation-or-permission), and [conflicting sources need an owner](/en/interview-lab/conflicting-sources-need-an-owner).

## Scope note

This is an AI.DOG single-question practice exercise. Its memory, users, policies, deletion, and results are fictional or synthetic draft fixtures. It is not privacy, retention, or legal advice, and it does not represent a deployed memory system or business outcome.
